In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LDV can infect any cell or cell line of any species in vitro when its RNA is introduced into the cell, whereas its replication in the cell is restricted by the cell type and the presence of MuLV.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the virus RNA is more important than the particles for the infection and replication of LDV in vitro, and the virus RNA can infect MuLV-infected or -noninfected cells or mouse macrophages irrespective of their age, but the virus particle can not.
the ability of LDV to infect cells is determined by its RNA and not by the particles.
LDV RNA is able to replicate in a wide variety of cell lines of various species, whereas LDV particles are able to enter and replicate only in a restricted cell population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the replication of LDV RNA in cells is not affected by their Fv-1 genotype and that the ability of the virus to replicate in cells is not related to the presence of the endogenous MuLV genome.
the infection of the virus is dependent on the type of the virus particles rather than the type of the cells.
LDV replication in cell lines is dependent on the introduction of its RNA into the cells.
